artifacts.summary: Rules on the phase-commit staging mechanism: --task alone cannot catch the observed undeclared-path case (proven by code trace of build_contended_manifest's >=2-declaring-task gate); ruling is both a now-implementable prose self-check (Containment against the task's own file_scope, drop-and-warn) across all fifteen recipes plus a recorded, out-of-scope follow-up mechanical check inside git-commit-scoped.sh coordinated with task 304.

memory_candidates.content: git-commit-scoped.sh's --task flag only engages the V5 contended-path lease for a path listed in specs/.contention-manifest/*.json, and build_contended_manifest (scripts/lib/territory-contention-lib.sh) only ever writes a path into that manifest when at least TWO tasks' own file_scope arrays declare it this cycle (uniq_tasks >= 2 gate). A path declared by zero tasks is therefore structurally invisible to --task under every possible value -- --task is an Overlap-family (sibling-vs-sibling) mechanism, not a Containment-family (one-path-vs-one-scope) one, per context/patterns/file-footprint-overlap.md's own vocabulary. Any defect shaped as 'an agent staged a path outside its OWN declared scope' needs a Containment check against that task's own file_scope, which --task does not and cannot provide.

A mid-dispatch, agent-issued phase commit (git-commit-scoped.sh called directly from inside an implementation agent's own recipe, not from orchestrator-postflight.sh or orchestrate-cycle-postflight.sh) has no postflight in scope and no guarantee that specs/.contention-manifest/ still reflects the current cycle -- that manifest is built once, per /orchestrate cycle, in orchestrate-cycle-plan.sh, before the dispatch loop, and a long-running implement dispatch can outlive several other tasks' cycles. Any scope/contention check for this specific layer must therefore be self-contained (re-derive from specs/state.json directly, or live inside git-commit-scoped.sh itself) rather than assume a freshly-built cycle manifest exists.
